stem: What is a company's authorised share capital?

options.content: The maximum nominal value of shares it is allowed to issue
options.rationale: Correct: it is a limit set by the constitution.

options.content: The total value of shares that have been paid for by shareholders
options.rationale: That is the issued and paid-up capital.

options.content: The market value of all its shares on the stock exchange
options.rationale: That is the market capitalisation.

options.content: The shares that the directors own personally
options.rationale: Authorised capital is not about who holds shares.

explanation: Authorised capital is the maximum the company may issue; only the issued shares are in the statement of financial position.

stem: Which of the following is a capital reserve?

options.content: Share premium
options.rationale: Correct: it arises from selling shares above their nominal value.

options.content: Retained earnings
options.rationale: These come from retained profits, so they are a revenue reserve.

options.content: General reserve
options.rationale: It is a transfer of retained profits, a revenue reserve.

options.content: Interim dividend
options.rationale: A dividend is a distribution, not a reserve.

explanation: Share premium and the revaluation reserve are capital reserves; retained earnings and the general reserve are revenue reserves.

stem: In which statement are the dividends of a company shown as a deduction?

options.content: The statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Dividends are not an expense.

options.content: The statement of financial position only
options.rationale: Only an unpaid declared dividend appears there, as a liability.

options.content: The cash book only
options.rationale: The cash book records payment but not the deduction from equity.

options.content: The statement of changes in equity
options.rationale: Correct: they reduce retained earnings.

explanation: Dividends are a distribution of profit and reduce retained earnings in the statement of changes in equity.

stem: A final dividend was declared on 15 December and remained unpaid at the year end of 31 December. How is it shown at 31 December?

options.content: Only in a note to the accounts
options.rationale: That is for dividends recommended after the year end.

options.content: As an expense in the statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Dividends are not expenses.

options.content: As an addition to retained earnings
options.rationale: It reduces retained earnings.

options.content: As a current liability
options.rationale: Correct: it had been declared, so the company owes it.

explanation: A dividend declared before the year end is a liability, so it is a current liability at that date and has already reduced retained earnings.
hints: Was there an obligation at the year end?

stem: A company transfers US\$12,000 from retained earnings to a general reserve. What is the effect on total equity?

options.content: It rises by US\$12,000, because a new reserve has been created in the books
options.rationale: A reserve is created, but retained earnings fall by the same amount.

options.content: There is no change, because one reserve rises and another falls by the same amount
options.rationale: Correct: no cash moves and total equity is the same.

options.content: It falls by US\$12,000, because cash is paid out
options.rationale: No cash is paid out.

options.content: It falls by US\$12,000, because the transfer is an expense
options.rationale: A transfer is not an expense.

explanation: A transfer between reserves leaves total equity unchanged; only the labels change.

stem: Which reserve cannot be used to pay a dividend?

options.content: Retained earnings, because they belong to the lenders
options.rationale: Retained earnings are distributable.

options.content: The general reserve, because it has been set aside
options.rationale: A general reserve is a revenue reserve and can be distributed.

options.content: The revaluation reserve, because the gain is unrealised
options.rationale: Correct: the asset has not been sold, so there is no realised profit.

options.content: All reserves, because dividends come only from cash
options.rationale: Dividends come from distributable profits, which are not the same as cash.

explanation: A revaluation gain has not been realised in cash, so the revaluation reserve is not distributable.

stem: A company has retained earnings of US\$36,000, a general reserve of US\$14,000, share premium of US\$34,000 and a revaluation reserve of US\$24,000. What is the largest dividend it may pay out of reserves?

options.rationale: This adds the capital reserves, which cannot be distributed.
This leaves out the general reserve, which is distributable.
Correct: retained earnings plus general reserve.
This adds the share premium, which is not distributable.

explanation: Distributable reserves are retained earnings 36,000 + general reserve 14,000 = 50,000; share premium and the revaluation reserve are not distributable.
hints: Which two reserves are revenue reserves?

stem: ZIMSEC style. What is the main feature of a preference share?

options.content: A right to vote on every matter in all circumstances
options.rationale: Preference shares usually carry limited voting rights.

options.content: A fixed rate of dividend that is paid before any ordinary dividend
options.rationale: Correct: the dividend has priority over the ordinary dividend.

options.content: A dividend that rises in line with the profit of the company
options.rationale: The dividend is fixed, not a share of the profit.

options.content: A claim that ranks behind the ordinary shares if the company closes
options.rationale: Preference shares rank before the ordinary shares.

explanation: Preference shares carry a fixed dividend which has priority over the ordinary dividend, and rank before ordinary shares on closure.

stem: Authorised share capital is included in the equity section of the statement of financial position.
explanation: False. Only the issued share capital forms part of equity; the authorised capital is shown in a note.

stem: A final dividend recommended by the directors after the year end is a liability at the year end.
explanation: False. There was no obligation at the year end; the dividend is disclosed in a note.
hints: Was it declared before the year end?

stem: Match each item to its type.
explanation: Share premium and the revaluation reserve are capital reserves (the latter from an unrealised gain); retained earnings are a revenue reserve; share capital is not a reserve.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: Only {{blank:a}} share capital forms part of equity. A dividend is a distribution of {{blank:b}} and is not an expense.

explanation: Issued shares are in equity; a dividend is a share of profit.

stem: What name is given to the amount by which the issue price of a share exceeds its nominal value?
explanation: It is the share premium, a capital reserve.

stem: A company has 350,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 each in issue. It pays an interim dividend of 3 cents per share. Calculate the total dividend paid.
explanation: 350,000 × US\$0.03 = US\$10,500. Using 3 dollars per share would give US\$1,050,000.
workedSolution: 1. 350,000 × US\$0.03 = US\$10,500. Using 3 dollars per share would give US\$1,050,000.

stem: A company's retained earnings were US\$61,300 at 1 January. The profit for the year was US\$47,800. The directors transferred US\$7,500 to a general reserve, paid an interim dividend of US\$9,500 and declared a final dividend of US\$12,500 before the year end. Calculate retained earnings at 31 December.
hints: Deduct the transfer and both dividends.

stem: A company has issued ordinary share capital of US\$180,000, share premium of US\$24,000, a revaluation reserve of US\$15,000, a general reserve of US\$9,000 and retained earnings of US\$52,500. Its authorised share capital is US\$220,000. Calculate total equity.
explanation: 180,000 + 24,000 + 15,000 + 9,000 + 52,500 = 280,500. The authorised capital is a note and is not added.
workedSolution: 1. 180,000 + 24,000 + 15,000 + 9,000 + 52,500 = 280,500. The authorised capital is a note and is not added.

stem: ZIMSEC style. A company has issued 80,000 7% preference shares of US\$1 each. Calculate the annual preference dividend.
explanation: 7% × US\$80,000 = US\$5,600. The dividend is a fixed percentage of the nominal value.
workedSolution: 1. 7% × US\$80,000 = US\$5,600. The dividend is a fixed percentage of the nominal value.
hints: The rate is applied to the nominal value.

stem: Explain why a company is not allowed to pay a dividend out of its share premium.

points.description: The share premium is a capital reserve, not a profit made from trading
It protects creditors, who rely on the capital of the company not being returned to the owners

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Share premium is capital contributed by shareholders, not profit. Keeping it in the company protects the creditors.

explanation: One mark for capital not profit and one for the protection of creditors.

stem: Explain the difference between an interim dividend and a final dividend and how each is treated at the year end.

points.description: An interim dividend is paid during the year; a final dividend is recommended after the year end and approved at the annual general meeting
A paid interim dividend reduces retained earnings and cash
A final dividend declared before the year end and unpaid is a current liability
A final dividend recommended after the year end is only a note, not a liability

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An interim dividend is paid during the year and reduces retained earnings and cash. A final dividend is approved after the year end; if declared before the year end and unpaid it is a current liability, but if recommended later it is only a note.

explanation: One mark for each of the four points.
hints: Ask whether there was an obligation at the year end.

stem: The directors of a company with a retained earnings balance of US\$18,000 and a revaluation reserve of US\$54,000 propose to pay a dividend of US\$35,000, arguing that total reserves are US\$72,000. Advise the directors.

points.description: The revaluation reserve is not distributable because the gain is unrealised
Only retained earnings of US\$18,000 (and any general reserve) are distributable
A dividend of US\$35,000 is more than the distributable reserves
Paying it would return capital to the owners at the expense of the creditors
Recommendation: pay no more than US\$18,000, or wait until the profit has been realised

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The revaluation reserve cannot be distributed because the gain is unrealised. Distributable reserves are only US\$18,000, so a dividend of US\$35,000 would return capital to the owners at the creditors' expense. The directors should pay no more than US\$18,000.

explanation: One mark each for the unrealised gain, the distributable limit, the comparison, the creditors and the recommendation.
hints: Which of the two reserves can be distributed?

parts.stem: Explain why the revaluation reserve is not available for distribution, and why the authorised share capital is not part of equity.

points.description: The revaluation gain is unrealised: the asset has not been sold
Distributing it would return capital to the owners at the expense of the creditors
Authorised share capital is only the maximum number of shares the company may issue
Only issued shares represent money contributed by the shareholders

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The revaluation gain has not been realised in cash and distributing it would harm creditors. The authorised capital is just a limit; only issued shares are contributed capital and part of equity.

stem: Masvingo Crafts Ltd has 200,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 each, fully paid. At 1 January 2025 its share premium was US\$22,000, its general reserve US\$15,000 and its retained earnings US\$48,000. During 2025 the profit for the year was US\$36,500. The directors transferred US\$5,000 to the general reserve, paid an interim dividend of 3 cents per share and declared a final dividend of US\$8,000 before the year end. The final dividend was unpaid at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How is the final dividend shown at 31 December 2025?

options.content: Only in a note to the accounts
options.rationale: It is a note only if recommended after the year end.

options.content: As an expense in the statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Dividends are not expenses.

options.content: As a current liability of US\$8,000
options.rationale: Correct: it was declared before the year end and is unpaid.

options.content: As a non-current liability
options.rationale: It is due within a year.

parts.explanation: A dividend declared before the year end and unpaid is a current liability.

To show that the amount is not intended for distribution, so it supports the confidence of lenders
